Everyday Situations.prompt: Set the scene: a friend is visiting the student's town on Saturday and likes food and outdoor activities but dislikes museums. Ask them to choose a morning activity, a lunch place, and an afternoon activity, then have them explain where they'd go, what they'd do, and why their friend would like it.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Student gives a plan for 3 parts of the day and uses 'going to' with at least one reason.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Explain that the student's friend always has a bad morning and needs a better routine. Encourage the student to choose solutions for waking up late, forgetting things, and having no breakfast, then have them say what their friend should do first, what they can change, and why it helps.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Student uses 'should' or 'can' for each problem and gives a reason.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Tell the student their friend is visiting and doesn't eat meat or like spicy food. Ask them to plan a meal, a drink, and something extra, then find out what they'd prepare and why they chose it.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Student names 3 food items and explains why each is suitable.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Present a change of plan: the student had a day outside planned, but now it's raining. Invite them to choose a new activity at home, a food or drink, and something fun to do, then have them explain their new plan and why it's better.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Student describes a new 3-part plan and gives one reason why it is better.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Set up a situation where a visitor is new in the student's town and needs help getting somewhere. Ask the student to choose a destination, transport, and route, then find out where the visitor goes, how they get there, and what they need.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Student gives clear directions including destination, transport, and one practical detail.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Explain that the student is organising a party for five friends on a small budget. Have them choose a place, food, and activities, then discuss their plan and why they chose these things.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Student names 3 plan items and gives at least one reason related to budget.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Tell the student they need to buy a birthday present for a friend with €20. Ask them to choose a present, a shop, and a reason, then find out what they'd buy and why their friend would like it.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Student names the present, the shop, and gives a clear reason the friend will like it.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Explain that the student's friend feels tired every day and needs a better routine. Encourage them to choose a food change, an activity, and a sleep habit, then have them say what their friend should do and why it helps.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Student gives 3 routine changes and a reason for at least one.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Set up a two-day trip with only a small bag to pack. Ask the student to choose three things to pack, transport, and one activity, then find out what they'd take and why these things matter.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Student lists 3 packed items and explains why each is important.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Explain that a new student has started at the school and needs to feel comfortable. Ask the student to explain important places, useful things to know, and advice for the first day.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Student gives at least 2 pieces of advice using 'should' or 'can'.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Tell the student their friend is moving to a new apartment and needs help choosing the best place. Ask them to choose a location, rooms, and important features, then discuss why the apartment is good and what their friend can do there.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Student uses at least 2 adjectives and gives one reason the apartment suits the friend.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Explain that the student's friend wants to spend one day without their phone. Invite the student to create the plan by choosing a morning, afternoon, and evening activity, then have them explain what their friend would do and why it's a good idea.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Student plans 3 parts of the day and gives one reason it is good.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Tell the student their friend starts a new job tomorrow and needs help. Ask them to explain what their friend needs, what they do in the morning, and what they take with them.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Student gives clear advice covering preparation, morning routine, and items to bring.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Set up a scenario where the student is choosing a restaurant for three friends with different needs — one vegetarian, one on a budget, one who loves desserts. Ask them where they'd go, what each person would eat, and why.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Student addresses all 3 friends' needs and explains the choice.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Explain that the student wants a fun weekend but doesn't have much money. Ask them to choose an activity, food, and transport, then find out their plan and how they save money.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Student gives a 3-part plan and explains how at least one thing saves money.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Set up a situation where a tourist is visiting the student's town and needs help. Ask the student to explain where the tourist should go, what they should see, and how they should travel.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Student uses 'should' to give at least 2 recommendations with a reason.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Tell the student they have an important day tomorrow — a birthday, first day at school, or meeting new people. Ask them to choose one and plan their clothes, food, and preparation, then have them explain what they'll do and why.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Student describes 3 preparations using 'going to' and gives at least one reason.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Explain that there's a problem at the student's home — no internet, a broken light, or no hot water. Ask them to choose one and tell you what the problem is, what they do about it, and who helps.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Student states the problem clearly, describes one action, and names who helps.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Explain that the student is shopping for food for one week. Ask them to choose breakfast, lunch, and dinner food, then find out what they'd buy and why.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Student names food for all 3 meals and gives one reason for a choice.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Tell the student their friend wants to improve their English and needs a simple plan. Ask them to choose a practice activity, time of day, and place, then have them explain what their friend would do and why it helps.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Student gives a complete 3-part practice plan and explains why it helps.

Describe.prompt: Ask the student to describe their bedroom, covering the furniture, the colours, and their favourite thing in it.
Describe.constraint: Student describes at least 3 features of the room using 'There is/are' or 'It has'.

Describe.prompt: Explore the student's kitchen at home — ask what's there, where things are, and what they use every day.
Describe.constraint: Student names at least 3 items and uses 'There is/are' or 'I use'.

Describe.prompt: Have the student describe a park near their home, covering what's there, what people do, and what they like about it.
Describe.constraint: Student names 3 features of the park and gives one opinion.

Describe.prompt: Ask the student to describe their classroom — the furniture, what's on the walls, and where they sit.
Describe.constraint: Student describes at least 3 features using 'There is/are'.

Describe.prompt: Find out about the student's favourite shop: what it sells, what it looks like, and why they like it.
Describe.constraint: Student describes what the shop sells and gives one reason they like it.

Describe.prompt: Invite the student to describe their school bag, covering what's inside, what they use every day, and one unusual item.
Describe.constraint: Student names at least 3 items inside and uses 'There is/are' or 'I keep'.

Describe.prompt: Ask the student to describe their fridge at home — what's inside, what they eat every day, and something they don't like.
Describe.constraint: Student names at least 3 food items and uses 'There is/are'.

Describe.prompt: Explore the student's desk or study space: what's on it, what they keep near them, and what they use most.
Describe.constraint: Student names at least 3 items and uses 'I keep' or 'I use'.

Describe.prompt: Have the student describe their wardrobe or cupboard — what's inside, their favourite clothes, and something they never wear.
Describe.constraint: Student names at least 3 items of clothing and uses 'There is/are'.

Describe.prompt: Ask the student to describe their pencil case, covering what's inside, what they use every day, and their favourite pen or pencil.
Describe.constraint: Student names at least 3 items inside and gives one preference.

Describe.prompt: Encourage the student to compare their home and their school — what's similar, what's different, and where they prefer to be.
Describe.constraint: Student gives at least one similarity and one difference between the two places.

Describe.prompt: Invite the student to compare their summer clothes and winter clothes — what they wear, the colours, and what they prefer.
Describe.constraint: Student compares at least 2 items of clothing and gives one preference.

Describe.prompt: Ask the student to compare their bedroom now with their bedroom as a child — what's different, what's the same, and what they miss.
Describe.constraint: Student gives at least 2 differences between the two bedrooms.

Describe.prompt: Discuss a weekday versus a weekend with the student — what they do, what they eat, and how they feel.
Describe.constraint: Student compares at least 2 activities between the two days.

Describe.prompt: Have the student compare their house and a friend's house — size, rooms, and what they like about each.
Describe.constraint: Student gives at least one similarity and one difference and names one thing they like.

Describe.prompt: Ask the student to describe their favourite jacket — what it looks like, where they got it, and when they wear it.
Describe.constraint: Student describes appearance, origin, and when they use the item.

Describe.prompt: Find out about the student's favourite mug or cup — what it looks like, where they got it, and why they like it.
Describe.constraint: Student describes appearance and gives one reason they like the item.

Describe.prompt: Invite the student to describe their favourite gadget — what it looks like, what they use it for, and how often they use it.
Describe.constraint: Student describes appearance and explains what the item is used for.

Describe.prompt: Ask the student to describe their favourite book or comic — what it looks like, what it's about, and why they like it.
Describe.constraint: Student describes the item and gives one reason for liking it.

Describe.prompt: Explore the student's favourite pair of shoes — what they look like, where they got them, and when they wear them.
Describe.constraint: Student describes appearance, origin, and when they wear the item.

Describe.prompt: Have the student describe a photo or picture in their home — what's in it, where it is, and why they keep it.
Describe.constraint: Student describes at least 2 details in the picture and gives one reason.

Describe.prompt: Ask the student to describe their phone case, covering the colour, the design, and why they chose it.
Describe.constraint: Student describes colour and design and gives one reason for the choice.

Describe.prompt: Invite the student to describe a plant in their home or garden — what it looks like, where it is, and who looks after it.
Describe.constraint: Student describes appearance and location and names who cares for it.

Describe.prompt: Explore an object on the student's desk right now — what it looks like, what's next to it, and what they use it for.
Describe.constraint: Student describes appearance, one neighbouring object, and its use.

Describe.prompt: Ask the student to describe a poster or picture on their wall — what colour it is, what's in it, and why they have it.
Describe.constraint: Student describes colour and content and gives one reason for having it.

Describe.prompt: Turn it into a guessing game: ask the student to describe an animal without saying its name, covering what it looks like, where it lives, and what it eats, then try to guess it.
Describe.constraint: Student gives at least 3 clues without naming the animal.

Describe.prompt: Play a guessing game: invite the student to describe a job without saying its name, covering what the person wears, where they work, and what they do, then try to guess it.
Describe.constraint: Student gives at least 3 clues without naming the job.

Describe.prompt: Set up a guessing game: ask the student to describe a food without saying its name, covering its colour, how it tastes, and when they eat it, then try to guess it.
Describe.constraint: Student gives at least 3 clues without naming the food.

Describe.prompt: Try a guessing game: have the student describe a place in town without saying its name, covering what you can do there, what's inside, and who goes there, then guess what it is.
Describe.constraint: Student gives at least 3 clues without naming the place.

Describe.prompt: Close with a guessing game: invite the student to describe an object in the kitchen without saying its name, covering what it looks like, what it's used for, and where it's kept, then try to guess it.
Describe.constraint: Student gives at least 3 clues without naming the object.

Explain and Show.prompt: Ask the student to teach you how to make their favourite drink — coffee, tea, juice, or a smoothie. Find out what you need, what to do first, and what happens next.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student names the ingredients and describes at least 2 steps in order using 'First' and 'Then'.

Explain and Show.prompt: Have the student show you their morning routine. Ask what time they wake up, what they do first, and what they do before leaving home.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student describes at least 3 actions in order using sequencing words.

Explain and Show.prompt: Invite the student to teach you how to use their favourite app — a messaging app, a video app, a game, or a music app. Find out what it's for, what you can do with it, and what you should try first.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student explains the app's purpose and gives at least 2 simple instructions.

Explain and Show.prompt: Ask the student to teach a visitor how to get around their town — to a restaurant, shop, park, or station. Have them show you how to get there, what transport to use, and what you need to know.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student gives clear directions with at least one transport method and one landmark.

Explain and Show.prompt: Have the student teach you a simple recipe — a sandwich, salad, breakfast, or dessert. Ask what ingredients you need, what to do first, and how to finish.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student lists at least 2 ingredients and describes the steps in order.

Explain and Show.prompt: Ask the student to show you how they prepare for work or school. Find out what they prepare, what they take with them, and what they do before leaving.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student names at least 3 things and describes the order of preparation.

Explain and Show.prompt: Invite the student to teach you a hobby — a sport, game, craft, or activity. Ask what you'd need, how to start, and what to do next.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student names the equipment needed and explains at least 2 steps to begin.

Explain and Show.prompt: Have the student show you how to have a good weekend by creating a plan. Ask what they do on Saturday, what they do on Sunday, and what the best part is.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student describes one activity for each day and gives a reason for the best part.

Explain and Show.prompt: Ask the student to teach you how to buy something in their country — food, clothes, a ticket, or a gift. Find out where to go, what to say, and what happens.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student describes the location, one useful phrase, and the process in order.

Explain and Show.prompt: Invite the student to show you how they relax after a busy day by creating their routine. Ask what they do first, what they do next, and what makes them feel good.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student describes at least 2 steps in order and gives one reason it helps.

Explain and Show.prompt: Ask the student to teach you how to look after something — a plant, a pet, a bike, or a phone. Find out what it needs, what they do, and how often.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student names at least 2 care actions and states how often each happens.

Explain and Show.prompt: Have the student show you how they get ready for a trip. Ask what they pack, what they check, and what they do before leaving.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student names at least 3 preparation steps in a clear order.

Explain and Show.prompt: Ask the student to teach you how to celebrate a special day — a birthday, holiday, festival, or family event. Find out what happens, what food people have, and what people do.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student describes the event with at least 3 details, including food and an activity.

Explain and Show.prompt: Invite the student to teach you how to set the table for a meal. Ask what you need, where everything goes, and what to do first.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student names at least 3 items and describes their positions or order.

Explain and Show.prompt: Have the student show you how to pack a bag for school or work. Ask what goes in first, what else they add, and what they check before leaving.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student describes packing in order using 'First', 'Then', and 'Finally'.

Explain and Show.prompt: Ask the student to teach you how to wash and dry laundry. Find out what they do first, what happens next, and how they finish.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student explains at least 3 steps in the correct order.

Explain and Show.prompt: Invite the student to show you how to make a hot drink for a guest. Ask what they'd say to the guest, what they prepare, and how they serve it.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student describes at least 2 steps and one polite phrase used with a guest.

Explain and Show.prompt: Have the student teach you how to use public transport in their town — bus, train, tram, or taxi. Ask where to buy a ticket, how to know where to get on, and what to do on arrival.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student explains at least 3 steps of the process in order.

Explain and Show.prompt: Ask the student to show you how to find their way to a new place — a friend's house, a shop, an office, or a school. Find out what to look for, which way to go, and how they know they've arrived.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student gives directions with at least 2 landmarks or turns.

Explain and Show.prompt: Invite the student to teach you how to cook eggs — fried, boiled, scrambled, or omelette. Ask what you need, what to do first, and how to know it's ready.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student names ingredients and describes at least 2 steps in order.

Explain and Show.prompt: Have the student show you how they organise their desk or bag. Ask what goes where, what they keep close, and why it's a good system.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student describes at least 2 organisation choices and gives one reason.

Explain and Show.prompt: Ask the student to teach you how to plan a shopping trip. Find out what goes on their list, where they go first, and how they save time or money.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student names at least 2 items and describes one practical tip.

Explain and Show.prompt: Invite the student to show you how they charge and look after their phone. Ask when they charge it, what they check, and what they avoid.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student describes at least 2 habits using present simple.

Explain and Show.prompt: Have the student teach you a simple exercise routine — stretching, walking, a home workout, or yoga. Ask how they start, what they do next, and how they finish.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student describes at least 3 steps in order using sequencing words.

Explain and Show.prompt: Ask the student to show you how they make their bed. Find out what they do first, what they do next, and how they finish.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student describes the process in at least 2 clear steps.

Explain and Show.prompt: Invite the student to teach you how to plan a birthday surprise for a friend. Ask what they prepare, who helps them, and what happens on the day.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student names at least 2 preparations and describes what happens on the day.

Explain and Show.prompt: Have the student show you how they take care of their health every day. Ask what they eat or drink, what activity they do, and what helps them sleep well.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student names at least 3 daily habits using present simple.

Explain and Show.prompt: Ask the student to teach you how to send a message or email politely. Find out how they start, what they write, and how they finish.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student describes at least 2 steps and one polite phrase.

Explain and Show.prompt: Invite the student to show you how to prepare a simple picnic. Ask what food they bring, what else they pack, and where they go.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student names at least 3 items and one location detail.

Explain and Show.prompt: Have the student teach you how to look after a house plant. Ask where they put it, how often they water it, and what else it needs.
Explain and Show.constraint: Student gives at least 2 care instructions using present simple.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay where you're the café worker and the student is a customer. Their goal is to order a drink — coffee, tea, juice, or water — and a snack such as cake, a sandwich, or salad. Ask them what they'd like and whether they want anything else, then explore why they chose it and what they usually order.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student orders one drink and one food item and answers at least one extension question.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Play the hotel receptionist while the student checks in for a holiday. Their goal is to get a room — single, double, or family — for one night, three nights, or one week. Find out who they're travelling with and what they need in the room.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student states room type and length of stay, and answers at least one extension question.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Take the role of a shop assistant while the student looks for something to wear — a shirt, jacket, shoes, or trousers, in black, blue, or white. Ask them when they'd wear it and how much it costs.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student names the item and colour they want and answers at least one extension question.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Play the doctor's receptionist while the student calls to make an appointment for a cold, headache, or stomach ache, choosing a morning, afternoon, or evening slot. Ask how they feel and what they do to feel better.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student explains the problem, chooses a time, and answers at least one extension question.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Act as someone who knows the area while the student asks for directions to a supermarket, station, restaurant, or park. Have them ask where it is and how to get there, then find out whether they'd walk or take transport and how long it takes.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student names a place and asks for directions using both questions, then answers one extension question.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Play the student's friend while they ask for help moving to a new home — books, clothes, furniture, or boxes. Get them to describe part of a plan (what to move first, when, who can help), then ask why they need help and what's difficult.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student names items to move, describes part of a plan, and answers at least one extension question.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Take the role of a supermarket worker while the student looks for fruit, milk, bread, or cheese. Have them ask where an item is and how much it costs, then find out what they buy every week and what they eat at home.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student names at least two items and asks both questions, then answers one extension question.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Play the student's friend while they plan a birthday party together — a place (home, park, or restaurant) and food (pizza, cake, or sandwiches). Ask who's coming and what time it starts.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student chooses a place and food and answers at least one extension question.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Act as the information desk worker while the student buys a train ticket to a city, beach, or airport for the morning, afternoon, or evening. Find out who they're travelling with and how long the journey is.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student states a destination and time and answers at least one extension question.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Play a new neighbour meeting the student for the first time. Encourage them to introduce themselves and talk about their name, home, job or school, and hobbies, then ask what they do in their free time and how long they've lived there.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student talks about at least 3 of the 4 topics and answers one extension question.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Take the role of a shop worker while the student returns an item that's the wrong size, broken, or the wrong colour, and asks for an exchange or a refund. Ask why they don't want it and what they'd like instead.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student explains the problem, states the solution they want, and answers one extension question.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Play a restaurant worker while the student books a table for 2, 4, or 6 people at 7pm, 8pm, or 9pm. Ask what food they like and whether they need anything special.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student states number of people and a time, and answers at least one extension question.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Have the student ask you, as a friend, about weekend plans, choosing an activity — cinema, shopping, walking, or eating out — and a day, Saturday or Sunday. Find out why they want to do it and what time they'd meet.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student chooses an activity and a day and answers at least one extension question.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Play hotel reception while the student calls about a problem — no hot water, a noisy room, or the wrong room — and asks for a solution. Ask what they want the hotel to do and how serious the problem is.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student explains the problem clearly and answers at least one extension question.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Play the student's friend while they talk through preparing for their first day at a new school or job — clothes, bag, transport, or schedule. Ask what they're worried about and what they need tomorrow.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student describes at least 2 preparations and answers one extension question.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Take the role of a pharmacy worker while the student explains a health problem — a cold, cough, or headache — and asks for medicine, advice, or information. Ask how they feel and what they usually do when they're sick.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student explains the problem, states what they need, and answers one extension question.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Play a restaurant worker taking a delivery order while the student chooses food — pizza, burger, salad, or pasta — and a drink — water, juice, or cola. Ask what food they like and when they usually order.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student orders one food and one drink and answers at least one extension question.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Play the student's friend while they ask for help learning something new — cooking, English, sport, or technology. Ask why they want to learn it and when they'd like to start.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student names what they want to learn and answers at least one extension question.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Act as an airport information desk worker while the student asks about their flight — finding the gate, checking the time, or finding a place — and talks about their destination, time, or a problem. Ask where they're going and who they're travelling with.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student states one need and talks about at least 2 of the 3 topics, then answers one extension question.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Play the student's friend while they plan a day out together — visiting a city, shopping, going to the beach, or the park — at a chosen time of day. Ask what they need to take and what they want to do first.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student chooses an activity and time and answers at least one extension question.

Choose and Create.prompt: Ask the student to create a weekend plan, choosing a place — park, city, or beach — and an activity — walking, shopping, or eating out. Have them explain what they chose and why.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student chooses a place and an activity and gives one reason using 'because'.

Choose and Create.prompt: Invite the student to plan a day out with a friend, choosing a time, a place — museum, market, or cinema — and food — café, restaurant, or picnic. Find out their plan and why they chose it.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student plans all 3 parts and uses 'we can' or 'let's' at least once.

Choose and Create.prompt: Have the student create a birthday party plan, choosing a place, an activity — games, music, or cake — and a time. Ask them to explain their plan and why people will enjoy it.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student names 3 plan items and gives one reason.

Choose and Create.prompt: Ask the student to plan a simple school day — a first activity, lunch arrangements, and what they do after school. Have them explain their plan and why.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student describes all 3 parts of the day using simple present or 'going to'.

Choose and Create.prompt: Invite the student to create a breakfast menu for a small café, choosing food, drinks, and prices. Find out what they'd choose and why people would like it.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student names at least 2 food items, 1 drink, and gives a price for each.

Choose and Create.prompt: Have the student create a menu for a birthday party, choosing food, drinks, and extras like cake or snacks. Ask them what they'd choose and why people would like it.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student names 3 menu items and gives one reason using 'because'.

Choose and Create.prompt: Ask the student to design a picnic menu for a sunny day, choosing food, drinks, and extras. Have them explain what they'd pack and why it suits a picnic.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student names 3 items and explains why they suit a picnic.

Choose and Create.prompt: Invite the student to create a lunch menu for a small restaurant, choosing a main dish, a drink, and a dessert. Find out their menu and why customers would like it.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student names all 3 courses and gives one reason customers will like it.

Choose and Create.prompt: Explain that the student is going on a two-day trip. Have them choose 3 important items and 2 optional ones, then ask what they'd pack and why each item matters.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student lists 3 important items and gives a reason for each.

Choose and Create.prompt: Ask the student to pack a bag for one day at the beach, choosing important items and optional items. Find out what they'd take and why.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student names at least 3 items and gives one reason using 'because'.

Choose and Create.prompt: Have the student prepare a bag for the first day at a new job, choosing important and optional items. Ask what they'd take and why each item helps.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student lists 3 items and explains why each is useful.

Choose and Create.prompt: Explain that the student is moving to a new apartment. Ask them to choose the 3 most important things to take first and give a reason for each.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student names 3 items in order of importance and gives one reason.

Choose and Create.prompt: Invite the student to prepare for a sports activity this weekend — football, running, or swimming — choosing important and optional items. Find out what they'd take and why.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student chooses a sport, lists 2 items, and gives one reason.

Choose and Create.prompt: Ask the student to design a small bedroom, choosing furniture, colours, and where things go. Have them explain their design and why it's comfortable.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student names 3 items and explains why the room is comfortable.

Choose and Create.prompt: Have the student design a study area at home, choosing furniture, equipment, and where things go. Ask them to explain their design and why it helps them study.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student names 3 items and gives one reason each helps studying.

Choose and Create.prompt: Invite the student to design a small café, choosing tables and chairs, decoration, and music. Find out their design and why customers would like it.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student names 3 design choices and gives one reason customers will like it.

Choose and Create.prompt: Ask the student to design a shop window display, choosing products to show, colours, and decoration. Have them explain their design and why it attracts customers.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student names 3 elements and gives one reason it attracts customers.

Choose and Create.prompt: Present two hotels for a weekend trip — Hotel A, cheap, small, near the beach; Hotel B, expensive, big, in the city centre. Ask the student which they'd choose and why.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student names one hotel and gives 2 reasons for the choice.

Choose and Create.prompt: Compare two after-school activities with the student — a sports club or an art class. Find out which they'd choose and why it's better for them.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student chooses one option and gives at least one clear reason.

Choose and Create.prompt: Present two phones for a friend — Phone A, cheap, small screen, good battery; Phone B, expensive, big screen, good camera. Ask the student which they'd choose and why.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student names one phone and gives 2 reasons for the choice.

Choose and Create.prompt: Compare two restaurants for a family dinner — Restaurant A, cheap and fast food; Restaurant B, expensive, quiet, slow service. Have the student choose one and explain why it suits the family.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student chooses one restaurant and gives one reason using 'because'.

Choose and Create.prompt: Present two ways to travel to work — Option A, bus, cheap and slow; Option B, taxi, expensive and fast. Ask the student which they'd pick and why.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student picks one option and gives at least one reason.

Choose and Create.prompt: Ask the student to choose a birthday gift for a friend with a €20 budget, deciding on the gift, the shop, and their reason. Find out what they'd buy and why their friend will like it.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student names the gift, the shop, and gives one clear reason.

Choose and Create.prompt: Have the student plan a simple activity for a visiting family member, choosing the activity, place, and time. Ask them to explain their plan and why the person will enjoy it.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student names 3 plan details and gives one reason the person will enjoy it.

Choose and Create.prompt: Invite the student to create a small welcome plan for a new student at school, covering what to show them, what to tell them, and who helps them.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student gives at least 2 pieces of help using 'should' or 'can'.

Choose and Create.prompt: Ask the student to choose a helpful item for a visitor who's new in town — a map, a phone number, or a list of places — and give a reason. Find out what they'd give and why it helps.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student names one item and gives one clear reason it helps the visitor.

Choose and Create.prompt: Have the student plan a small surprise for a family member's special day, choosing an activity, food, and decoration. Ask them to explain their plan and why the person will like it.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student names 3 plan items and gives one reason using 'because'.

Choose and Create.prompt: Ask the student to create a shopping list for one week of dinners, choosing 5 food items and explaining why each is needed.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student lists 5 items and gives at least one reason.

Choose and Create.prompt: Invite the student to plan a simple exercise schedule for one week, choosing days, type of exercise, and time of day. Find out their schedule and why it works for them.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student gives a 3-part schedule and one reason it fits their life.

Choose and Create.prompt: Have the student create a simple morning routine for a busy weekday, choosing a first task, breakfast, and a last task before leaving. Ask them to explain their routine and why it saves time.
Choose and Create.constraint: Student describes all 3 steps and gives one reason it saves time.

Guided Stories.prompt: Ask the student to tell the story of losing their bag at the train station. Have them explain where they last had it, where they looked, and who helped them find it.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student uses First, Then, Finally and past tense to tell the story.

Guided Stories.prompt: Invite the student to tell the story of arriving late for an important meeting. Find out why they were late, what they did, and what happened when they arrived.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student gives a reason for being late and describes 3 story parts in order.

Guided Stories.prompt: Have the student tell the story of breaking a friend's phone by accident. Ask how it happened, what they said, and how they solved the problem.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student describes the accident, a reaction, and a solution using past tense.

Guided Stories.prompt: Ask the student to tell the story of forgetting their homework at home on the day it's due. Find out when they noticed, what they did, and how the problem ended.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student tells a 3-part story with a clear ending using First, Then, Finally.

Guided Stories.prompt: Invite the student to tell the story of getting a flat tyre far from home. Ask where they were, what they did, and how they got home.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student describes the problem and gives a clear solution in sequence.

Guided Stories.prompt: Have the student tell the story of a busy day at work or school, covering the morning, the afternoon, and how the day ends.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student describes 3 parts of the day using First, Then, Finally.

Guided Stories.prompt: Ask the student to tell the story of a special day, like a birthday or celebration, covering how it starts, what they do together, and how it finishes.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student sequences the day into 3 clear parts with past tense verbs.

Guided Stories.prompt: Invite the student to tell the story of a day trip to another city, covering how they travel, what they see or do, and how they return home.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student describes travel, activity, and return using sequence words.

Guided Stories.prompt: Have the student tell the story of a day when everything goes wrong, covering what happens first, what happens next, and how the day ends.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student describes at least 2 problems and gives an ending.

Guided Stories.prompt: Ask the student to tell the story of their first day at a new job or school. Find out how they felt arriving, what they did during the day, and how they felt at the end.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student uses First, Then, Finally and describes a feeling at start and end.

Guided Stories.prompt: Have the student build a story by choosing a place — park, shop, or train station — a person — friend, stranger, or family member — and a problem — lost item, wrong direction, or no money. Ask them to create the story using their choices.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student names all 3 choices and tells a complete story using them.

Guided Stories.prompt: Invite the student to build a story by choosing a place — restaurant, airport, or school — a person — teacher, classmate, or waiter — and an activity — ordering food, catching a flight, or giving a presentation. Have them create the story using their choices.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student includes all 3 chosen elements and uses First, Then, Finally.

Guided Stories.prompt: Ask the student to build a story by choosing a place — their house, a friend's house, or a hotel — a person — neighbour, visitor, or delivery person — and a problem — broken object, strange noise, or unexpected visitor. Have them create the story using their choices.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student uses all 3 chosen elements and completes a beginning, middle, and end.

Guided Stories.prompt: Have the student build a story by choosing a place — supermarket, gym, or library — a person — friend, stranger, or staff member — and an activity — helping someone, finding something, or meeting someone new. Ask them to create the story using their choices.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student combines the 3 choices into one clear story with a sequence.

Guided Stories.prompt: Invite the student to build a story by choosing a place — city street, bus stop, or office — a person — old friend, new colleague, or lost tourist — and a problem — bad weather, wrong bus, or forgotten appointment. Have them create the story using their choices.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student tells the story in order and uses all 3 chosen elements.

Guided Stories.prompt: Ask the student to imagine a park on a sunny afternoon. Have them describe where they are, what they see around them, and a small event that happens next.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student describes the scene and adds one event that happens.

Guided Stories.prompt: Invite the student to imagine a small shop on a quiet street. Ask them to describe where they are, the items and people in the shop, and a small event that happens next.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student describes the location, at least 2 details, and one event.

Guided Stories.prompt: Have the student imagine a busy street in the city at rush hour. Ask them to describe where they are, the people and traffic around them, and something unexpected that happens.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student sets the scene and describes one unexpected happening.

Guided Stories.prompt: Ask the student to imagine a cosy house on a rainy day. Have them describe where they are, the rooms and objects around them, and a small event that happens next.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student uses 'There is/are' to describe the scene and adds an event.

Guided Stories.prompt: Invite the student to imagine a train station early in the morning. Ask them to describe where they are, the people and things around them, and a small event that happens next.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student describes the setting with 2 details and one event.

Guided Stories.prompt: Explain that a friend can't find their way in a new city. Ask the student who needs help, what the problem is, and how they help their friend.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student identifies the problem and describes the help given, step by step.

Guided Stories.prompt: Explain that a new student doesn't know anyone at school. Ask the student who needs help, what the problem is, and how they help them.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student describes the problem and gives at least 2 actions that help.

Guided Stories.prompt: Explain that a visitor to the student's town doesn't speak the local language well. Ask who needs help, what the problem is, and how the student helps them.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student describes the problem and explains the help step by step.

Guided Stories.prompt: Explain that a family member forgets an important appointment and is late and worried. Ask the student who needs help, what the problem is, and how they help them.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student explains the problem and describes a clear solution.

Guided Stories.prompt: Explain that a friend's car breaks down on the way to work. Ask the student who needs help, what the problem is, and how they help them.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student uses First, Then, Finally to describe the help given.

Guided Stories.prompt: Ask the student to describe a messy room before and after cleaning — what it looked like, what changed, and what it looks like now.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student contrasts before and after using 'There was/were' and 'Now there is/are'.

Guided Stories.prompt: Invite the student to describe a trip before they left and after they returned — how they felt before, what happened on the trip, and how they feel now.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student describes a feeling before and after, with one event in between.

Guided Stories.prompt: Have the student describe learning a new skill, before and after practice — what they couldn't do, how they practised, and what they can do now.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student contrasts ability before and after using 'could' and 'can'.

Guided Stories.prompt: Ask the student to describe a garden or park before and after a change of season — what it looked like, what happened over time, and what it looks like now.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student describes 2 clear differences between before and after.

Guided Stories.prompt: Invite the student to describe their English before and after taking lessons — what they couldn't do, what they did to improve, and what they can do now.
Guided Stories.constraint: Student contrasts ability before and after using 'could' and 'can'.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Ask the student to imagine they can fix only one thing in their apartment this month. Find out what they'd choose and why.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Choose only one thing to fix.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Explore which internet plan the student would choose for their household — cheaper but slower, or faster but more expensive — and why.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Give at least one reason based on cost and one based on speed.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Ask the student to recommend what a friend should do about a car repair: one day but expensive, or one week but cheaper. Find out their reasoning.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Recommend only one option, based on their situation, not yours.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Discuss how the student would respond if a friend asked to borrow money until next month.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Your answer must address both the friendship and the money.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Invite the student to choose between two apartments — shorter commute but higher rent, or longer commute but lower rent — and justify their decision.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Mention at least one trade-off you're accepting.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Ask the student to recommend what to do about a roommate's higher-than-expected energy bill.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Recommend one specific action, not a list of possibilities.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Talk about how the student would plan meals for the week on a limited budget.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Mention at least two meals and one cost-saving decision.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Explore how the student would compromise between the cost of a school trip and their child's wishes.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Your compromise must involve a real trade-off, not a simple yes or no.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Find out how the student would spend two days off with a long list of errands, and their priorities.
Everyday Situations.constraint: You must leave at least one errand for later and explain why.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Ask the student to decide between a faster private appointment or a free public one with a long wait for a minor health problem, and explain their reasoning.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Base your decision on how the problem is affecting your daily life, not just the cost.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Discuss whether the student would fix an old washing machine or buy a new one, and why.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Mention cost and at least one other factor.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Ask the student to propose a compromise to their manager after a schedule change clashes with picking up their kids from school.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Your compromise must address both your needs and the company's.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Explore what the student would recommend to a family member choosing between two doctors — one sooner but further, one closer but with a longer wait.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Base your recommendation on urgency, not just distance.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Find out which monthly subscription the student would cancel, and why.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Choose only one subscription to cancel.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Ask the student what they'd recommend to a friend deciding whether to attend an expensive wedding abroad.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Your recommendation must balance cost against the value of the relationship.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Invite the student to choose between two neighbourhoods when moving to a new city — one convenient but noisy, one quiet but far from work.
Everyday Situations.constraint: You must weigh convenience against quality of life.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Discuss how the student's team could agree on a weekly meeting time that suits everyone.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Mention at least one compromise.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Ask the student to compare two jobs — one paying more with a long commute, one paying less but close to home — and explain which matters more to them.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Weigh at least two factors for each job before reaching a conclusion.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Explore how the student's family would prioritise factors — distance, reputation, cost, facilities — when choosing between two schools.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Rank at least three factors before naming your final choice.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Find out whether the student would take a better-paid job in a different city, even if it means leaving friends and family behind.
Everyday Situations.constraint: You must weigh the relationship cost against the professional opportunity, not just the money.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Ask the student how they'd manage if their internet stopped working and a technician couldn't come for five days.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Mention at least one practical workaround.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Discuss what matters most to the student in a new phone — price, reliability, or speed of getting one — and their final choice.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Rank your priorities before stating your decision.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Explore how the student would handle two friends asking for help moving house on the same weekend.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Your answer must address both friendships.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Ask the student how they'd vote on installing a new elevator that raises everyone's monthly fees.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Mention both the benefit and the cost.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Talk about whether the student would cook at home or eat out more, based on their schedule and budget.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Support your decision with a specific reason from your daily life.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Find out what the student would do about an expensive gym membership they rarely use.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Choose one specific action, not just 'I should think about it.'

Everyday Situations.prompt: Ask the student what they'd recommend to a neighbour choosing between two contractors — one cheaper with a longer wait, one pricier but available now.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Your recommendation must address both time and money.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Discuss how the student would handle a relative wanting to stay for two weeks in their small apartment while they work from home.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Your answer must consider both hospitality and practicality.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Explore whether the student would use public transport or buy a car, based on their daily needs.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Mention at least one cost and one convenience factor.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Ask the student how they'd vote on a local council choice between repairing roads or improving the park.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Your answer must consider the needs of the wider community, not just yourself.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: the student booked a hotel room online but arrives to find it's occupied. Play the front desk staff and have them negotiate a solution, given they have nowhere else to stay tonight.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student negotiates a workable solution and gives at least one reason to support their preferred outcome.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: the student's neighbour has played loud music for three nights and they have an early start tomorrow. Play the neighbour and have the student raise it and agree on a compromise.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student raises the issue politely and reaches a compromise using softened disagreement language.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: the student and a colleague both want the same week off work. Play the colleague and have them discuss reasons and reach a fair agreement.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student explains their reasons and works toward a fair agreement, acknowledging the colleague's position.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: a repair shop wants to charge more than the original quote to fix the student's laptop. Play the shop and have them negotiate the price, explaining what they can realistically afford.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student states the discrepancy, negotiates a new price, and justifies their budget limit.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: a furniture shop sent the student a sofa in the wrong colour and claims it was their mistake. Play the shop and have them explain why they believe the error was the shop's, and what they expect done.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student explains their position clearly, states evidence for their view, and states a desired outcome.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: the student's gym membership renewed automatically but they want a cheaper plan. Play the staff member and have them persuade you to make the change without a penalty fee.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student persuades the staff member using at least one polite persuasion phrase and a clear reason.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: a friend wants to split a restaurant bill equally, but the student only ordered a small dish while the friend ordered several courses. Play the friend and have them discuss a fair way to split it.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student proposes a fair alternative and reaches agreement with the friend.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: the student shares an apartment and their roommate keeps leaving dishes for days. Play the roommate and have them raise the issue and agree on a new system.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student resolves the conflict calmly and agrees on a concrete new system.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: the student needs to change a dentist appointment, but the only free slot clashes with an important work meeting. Play the receptionist and have them persuade you to find another solution.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student persuades the receptionist to offer an alternative, giving a clear reason for the request.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: a delivery driver left the student's package with a neighbour without telling them, and it's now missing. Play the neighbour and have them discuss the situation and decide what to do next.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student resolves the conflict calmly and agrees on a next step with the neighbour.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: the student wants a refund for a concert ticket because the event was postponed to a date they can't attend. Play the box office and have them try to convince you to help.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student persuades the box office using a clear reason and at least one persuasive phrase.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: the student and a friend are planning a weekend trip but disagree about the budget. Play the friend and have them work together to find a plan that suits both.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student proposes options and reaches agreement that addresses both budgets.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: the student's landlord wants to raise the rent, but the student feels the increase is too high given the apartment's condition. Play the landlord and have them discuss and try to reach a compromise.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student negotiates the increase and justifies their position with a specific reason.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: a colleague keeps taking credit for the student's ideas in meetings. Play the colleague and have the student calmly explain how they'd like things to change.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student explains their position clearly and states what change they would like to see.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: the student wants to return a jacket that no longer fits, but has lost the receipt. Play the shop assistant and have them try to persuade you to help anyway.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student persuades the shop assistant using a polite, reasoned argument.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: the student and a friend are choosing a restaurant for a group dinner but have very different budgets. Play the friend and have them find an option they can both agree on.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student proposes a compromise option and reaches agreement with the friend.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: the student's internet keeps cutting out, but the provider insists the problem is with their equipment. Play the provider and have them resolve the disagreement and agree on next steps.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student resolves the conflict by presenting their view and agreeing on next steps with the provider.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: the student's tutor has raised their lesson price with very little notice. Play the tutor and have the student explain whether the increase feels fair and how they'd like to move forward.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student explains their position clearly and states a preferred way forward.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: a mechanic recommends several repairs for the student's car, but the student suspects not all are necessary. Play the mechanic and have them persuade you to justify each recommendation.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student persuades the mechanic to justify each recommendation, using at least one probing question.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: the student and a family member disagree about which venue to book for a celebration. Play the family member and have them talk it through and reach a joint decision.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student proposes reasons for their preference and reaches a joint decision.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: a shop refuses to exchange a gift bought during a sale. Play the shop assistant and have the student explain their situation and try to find a solution.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student persuades the shop assistant with a clear explanation and a suggested solution.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: the student's flight was delayed and they missed a connecting train, but airline staff say it isn't their responsibility. Play the airline staff and have them resolve the disagreement.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student resolves the conflict by stating their case and negotiating what the airline will offer.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: the student wants to cancel their phone contract early, but the company wants a high cancellation fee. Play the company and have the student explain why the fee feels unfair.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student explains their position clearly and responds to the company's counter-proposal.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: a colleague wants to borrow money from the student, who isn't comfortable lending the full amount. Play the colleague and have them discuss the situation honestly and agree on a solution.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student explains their position honestly and reaches an agreement that respects their limits.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: the student is sharing a taxi with a stranger heading a similar direction, but their destinations aren't identical. Play the stranger and have them agree on a fair route and fare split.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student negotiates a fair route and cost split, giving at least one reason for their proposal.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: the student's child's school wants an extra fee for a trip they feel is too expensive. Play the staff member and have the student raise their concerns.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student explains their position clearly and states what outcome they are hoping for.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: a friend cancelled plans with the student last minute for the second time. Play the friend and have the student honestly discuss how this affects the friendship.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student resolves the conflict by expressing how they feel and working toward an understanding.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: the student wants to work from home two days a week, but their manager prefers everyone in the office. Play the manager and have the student present their case and find a compromise.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student negotiates a compromise and supports their case with at least one clear reason.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: the student's energy bill was unexpectedly high, and they and the provider disagree about the cause. Play the provider and have them work together to reach an agreement.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student works with the provider to reach an agreement on the cause and next steps.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Set up a roleplay: two neighbours disagree about who should pay for a shared fence that needs repairing. Play one neighbour and have the student discuss the situation and agree on a fair arrangement.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student negotiates a fair arrangement and justifies their proposed share of responsibility.

Describe.prompt: Ask the student to compare living in their current neighbourhood with another neighbourhood they know. Find out which suits them better, and why.

Describe.prompt: Show the student two photographs of the same street taken at different times of day. Find out which feels safer or more welcoming.

Describe.prompt: Ask the student to describe the customer service at a shop or restaurant they visit. Find out what works well, and what doesn't.

Describe.prompt: Ask the student to describe their home, or one they know well. Find out which room would benefit most from renovation, and why.

Describe.prompt: Talk about how the design of a website or app has changed over the years. Find out if the current version is easier to use.

Describe.prompt: Ask the student to compare two offices or classrooms they've worked or studied in. Find out which helps people concentrate more, and why.

Describe.prompt: Talk about how traffic or crowding has changed on a street the student knows well. Find out if it's better or worse now.

Explain and Show.prompt: Ask the student to explain what a friend should check before signing a lease on their first apartment, and why.

Explain and Show.prompt: Ask the student to explain how to use a train ticket machine to a confused tourist, and recommend the fastest option.
